subject.title: [Bug]: Slack replies ~2s slower than other channels — dominant cost is Socket Mode event delivery; channel-side stalls fixed in #101888

question: Should Slack setup/docs explicitly recommend HTTP Request URLs as the low-latency hosted transport, or should maintainers change Slack setup/default behavior beyond the existing `mode: "http"` support?
rationale: HTTP mode already exists and the remaining measured latency is mostly outside OpenClaw code, but stronger guidance or default changes affect setup expectations, ingress requirements, and operator support.

options.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
options.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default for local/private deployments and update Slack docs/setup guidance to prefer HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where reply latency matters.

options.title: Change setup/default behavior
options.body: Have maintainers sponsor a stronger Slack setup or default change that steers new hosted installs away from Socket Mode, with upgrade and operator guidance.

options.title: Accept current guidance
options.body: Record that the existing transport table is sufficient and close after deciding no extra latency-specific docs or setup change is planned.

recommendation.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
recommendation.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default for local/private deployments and update Slack docs/setup guidance to prefer HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where reply latency matters.

likelyOwner.reason: They produced the measurements, authored the merged partial fix, and scoped the remaining work to HTTP mode guidance.
